questions.question: Define a need and a want and give two examples of each.
questions.expected_answer: Need: something essential for survival and a decent life, e.g. food, water, shelter, clothing, health care, safety. Want: something desired but not essential, e.g. takeaways, branded clothing, newest smartphone, holidays.

questions.question: Explain, with an example, why the same item can be a need for one person and a want for another.
questions.expected_answer: Needs depend on circumstances. E.g. a car is a want for most city families with public transport but a need for a district nurse who must reach patients far from public transport; spectacles are a need for someone with poor eyesight.

questions.question: Give two basic needs each for a family, a community and the country, and explain one link between the levels.
questions.expected_answer: Family: a home, an income, food, care. Community: clinic, school, roads, water, refuse removal, police. Country: defence, electricity, ports and railways, courts, jobs. Link e.g.: if national electricity fails, community clinics and family homes are affected; a growing economy gives families income to meet their needs.
